Bethesda says there are "currently no plans" for paid Fallout 4 mods

Well that's a bit ominous.. I would have hoped they'd learned what the community thinks of that idea after the last round. But it would probably be easier to implement something like that on a brand new game with a modding community that is not yet established and used to the free stuff.

If they do go with paid mods, I really hope they do some sort of curation. The last experiment with free-for-all paid mods turned into a scam-fest real quick. I would not be opposed to Zenimax/Bethesda procuring some of the better mods, paying the modders to polish it up and then releasing it as a pack/dlc.

I hate to play devils advocate, but I feel like mod makers deserve money in some way. We had this exact issue 6-8 years ago with Youtubers, people felt like they didn't deserve money because their content was just "a hobby". It really sucks because with Youtubers it was a bit simpler, they could make money off adds, but with mod makers they can't really do quite the same.

Personally I hope something is figured out, mod makers have made mods far better than some dlc's.
I think the best way would be to implement a quick and easy way to donate to the mod-creators.
I agree and i think a good way to do it is for bethesda to hire modders for their expansions etc.

Mods implementation should look like this:

Value 25% cut, Dev 25% cut, mod maker 50% cut.

When following a mod, a window should pop up with a slider. The slider should by default be in the middle, with a price set by the mod maker. The slider can be moved UP, to whatever number you want, or moved DOWN, all the way to ZERO (NOT ONE DOLLAR!)

This is the only way I would ever support paid mods.

If more effort was put into the paid mods system, not on the modders parts who tried to work with the system Steam mand Zenimax laid out them themselves. If they'd made it so they took a small cut, maybe 15% for Zenimax and 5% for Steam, and then really opened it up so that modders could have the paid version the same as their free version but just with a thank you or something, and took out the stupid as fuck advertising in the game nonsense.

They fucked it all up, they were greedy and they didn't give the modders a big enough cut or enough time or power over their creations. It could have worked but the way they set it up was all for them and near enough nothing for the customers or the modders. I'm glad the system as it was failed, but if they were to try it again but this time make it more robust and beneficial to the community I'd take part in it. They'd have to tighten the rules up to "Only content YOU create can be included in your mod, although dependencies are allowed." So people couldn't use other's resources without requiring the relevant mod in the list as well. And then they'd have to fix the pricing issues and the way it's split.

Oh you can bet it's coming.. After the Oblivion debacle ZeniMax doubled down on making it work "in the future," so make peace with this cash grab happening. If the past is any indication they will wait until there is a sizable user base and flip the switch overnight. Greed will tickle the majority of modders pocketbooks and they'll put their work behind pay walls. Gamers will just have to deal with one of the fundamental community driven aspects of gaming fading away as publishers begin having them grab their ankles in turn once they see ZM reaping profit with minimal effort.
I've never regretted the decision to back away from gaming less. When I was younger and built my first PC expansion packs were almost a game into themselves. As I strode into mid-life and saw DLC come online I had a cynical eye and was hardly surprised as microtransactions become normative. Now we have paid mods to round out the field and massive publishers have never been more about the money.
